narrationScript: For our hands-on activity, you'll get a practical feel for these differences. Your task is to write a simple C program, for example, one that sums an array of integers. Then, you'll compile this program into assembly code for two different ISAs. You can use cross-compilers on your system, or more conveniently, an online tool like Godbolt, which allows you to compile C code to assembly for various targets like x86-64 and ARM64. Compare the generated assembly output. Pay close attention to the number of instructions, their lengths, how memory is accessed, and the usage of registers. This direct comparison will vividly illustrate the architectural philosophies we've discussed.
deliveryNotes: Explain the goal of the activity clearly
List specific points of comparison for the assembly code
